Shishuang Chuyuan owns the retained test: he asked a monk — newly arrived from where? — the sun is getting low — and pressed on: say the one line of no crossing by the road's stages — the monk: seven nines are sixty-three — 'just so' — 'you take my breath away' — and the master struck him.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (T/T47/T47n1997.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yuanwu Foguo. Yuanwu Keqin owns the retained address: the whole sky mild air, the ground brimming spring light, willow eyes burst open, mulberry twigs split their seams, blossom boughs like brocade, bird talk like reed pipes — the seal uncarved through eight holes, the unspeaking wonder-gate through a hundred heads, a thousand threads; cut it off on the spot and the dead fire does not reignite; trust it outright and the shoots rise beyond the withered roots — no crossing by the road's stages, set that aside: how would you say the mud-and-water line? returning home is all the children's affair — the grandfather never once goes out the gate.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J25/J25nB171.xml). Recorded Sayings of Monk Tianyin. Tianyin Yuanxiu owns the raised test: Langye Huijue asked elder Quan — newly arrived from where? — Liangzhe — by boat or by land? — by boat — where is the boat? — on foot below — then say the one line of no crossing by the road's stages — Quan struck his sitting cloth once: hack writers, elders thick as hemp and millet — and swept out his sleeves; Langye asked the attendant who it was, went down himself to the traveler's hall, begged pardon for the offense; Quan shouted, asked when the elder had reached Fenyang — I heard your name in Zhejiang long ago — and your insight turns out to be no more than this — Langye bowed: Huijue's fault.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J25/J25nB174.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Juelangsheng of Tianjie. Juelang Daosheng owns the retained charge: I do not know from where my two fellow heirs of Longmen and Xiansheng let out this poison and founded this refuge — in the charnel ground overturning the live-buried dead, on the rock pile cremating the unsupported men; a single stalk of grass raised into a Brahma-king's palace, and whoever enters this threshold at once cuts the stealing mind; a withered stump carved into a six-foot golden body, and whoever sees that light wholly escapes the sheath — whether they came by boat or by land or by no road's stages at all, each gets his three blows; and when buddha arrives and a founder arrives, in what admits no arranging he too must be given his portion — then the circle drawn: only one who gets his body out through here can digest this poison and make this school cover sky and earth — the ninety-thousand-li roc rises from the sea; the three-thousand-year crane returns far through the sky.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J26/J26nB178.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Feiyin. Feiyin Tongrong owns the retained ruling: the person's own affair crosses no road's stages — it is not the wondrous truth before your eyes, nor a talisman beyond the frame; therefore the law is the constant law, the way the constant way, the person the constant person, the self the constant self — see it so and, blow on blow, you pass beyond buddha and founder, pair by pair, kin and stranger both extinguished; pull off the single eye held up in the open and laugh at Yangqi's three-legged donkey.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J26/J26nB183.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Shiqi of Xuedou. Shiqi Tongyun owns the retained letter: your letter says you do not yet know the entry-path — hold this mind unforgetting, moment on moment, and an opening will come: only know your own mind outright, and there is no entering without self-winning, no ordinary, no holy, birth cut off, death cut off — entry-path, way-out: where would you set them? This affair has no deadline from the first; what is prized in a true great man is one straight cut of the knife, no crossing by the road's stages — catch it at a word, and you will face this poor cleric in person.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J35/J35nB336.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Huigong Kaixiong of Baoxianglin, Nanhai. The retained section carries the unit twice: Wufang Kecong's address — the upward school-vehicle has fundamentally no words; the person's one move is not borrowed from outside; it must burst from your own breast, leaning on no thing, setting up no dark — no crossing by the road's stages, and only then the steady seat at home — else: do you know Jiufeng's refusal of the seat? Baizhang's five hundred births in the fox den? the gold needle scraping the film — the moment you scheme, it misses; then Huigong Kaixiong's verdict verse: no road's stages — yet you must reach home; touch a dead snake and the trouble runs long.

Senses.Explanation: No crossing by the road's stages: the boat underfoot, the grandfather who never leaves the gate, three blows for those who came by no road — arrival without the journey. Shishuang Chuyuan, meeting a fresh arrival: newly come from where? the sun is getting low — then, say the one line of no crossing by the road's stages; the monk: seven nines are sixty-three — just so — you take my breath away — and the master struck him. Yuanwu Keqin, in the hall amid spring light: the seal uncarved through eight holes, the unspeaking wonder-gate through a hundred heads; cut it off on the spot and the dead fire does not reignite; trust it outright and the shoots rise beyond the withered roots — no crossing by the road's stages, set that aside: how would you say the mud-and-water line? returning home is all the children's affair; the grandfather never once goes out the gate. Tianyin Yuanxiu, raising the old test for the assembly: Langye Huijue asked elder Quan — by boat or by land? — by boat — where is the boat? — on foot below — then say the no-road line — Fahua Quanju struck his sitting cloth once: hack writers, elders thick as hemp and millet — and swept out his sleeves; Langye went down to the traveler's hall to beg pardon and got a shout, then heard his own fame priced and bowed: Huijue's fault. Juelang Daosheng, over the funeral refuge his fellow heirs founded: a single stalk of grass raised into a Brahma-king's palace, a withered stump carved into a six-foot golden body — whether they came by boat or by land or by no road's stages at all, each gets his three blows; and when a buddha arrives and a founder arrives, in what admits no arranging he too must be given his portion. Feiyin Tongrong, at the small meeting: the person's own affair crosses no road's stages — not the wondrous truth before your eyes, not a talisman beyond the frame; the law is the constant law, the way the constant way, the person the constant person, the self the constant self — see it so and you pass beyond buddha and founder; pull off the single eye held up in the open and laugh at Yangqi's three-legged donkey. Shiqi Tongyun, writing to the layman who says he has not yet found the entry-path: hold this mind unforgetting and an opening will come — only know your own mind outright, no ordinary, no holy, birth cut off, death cut off; what is prized in a true great man is one straight cut of the knife, no crossing by the road's stages — catch it at a word, and you will face this poor cleric in person. Huigong Kaixiong, keeping his forebear's address and sealing it with a verse: the upward school-vehicle has no words; the person's one move is not borrowed from outside; it must burst from your own breast — no crossing by the road's stages, and only then the steady seat at home; and the verse sets the bar: no road's stages — yet you must reach home; touch a dead snake and the trouble runs long.
